claims.text: Data written to a volume's mount path goes into the volume, not the container's writable layer; removing the container leaves a named volume in place, and a new container mounting it at the same path sees the data.
A named volume is managed by Docker; a bind mount shows an existing host file or folder at a chosen container path and is tied to that host path.

In docker-compose.yml@stage-1 the db service mounts db-data at /var/lib/postgresql/data and bind-mounts db/schema.sql and db/seed.sql into /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/ (read-only); named volumes are declared under the top-level volumes: key.
The postgres image runs scripts in /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d only when the data directory is empty; with an existing db-data they are skipped.
claims.source_hint: postgres image docs (Docker Hub: Initialization scripts)

claims.text: Compose prefixes named volumes with the project name (name: donhang), so db-data is donhang_db-data; the lab service bind-mounts ./ at /repo read-only.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: docker-compose.yml name: donhang, lab.volumes; docker volume ls on the running lab

claims.text: docker compose rm -sf db stops and removes donhang-db, docker volume ls still lists donhang_db-data, and docker compose up -d --wait db starts a new container with the same order count.
claims.source_hint: generator check on the running lab (25 orders before and after; API answered 200 afterwards)

claims.text: psql -t prints tuples only, -A unaligned output, -c runs one command.
A volume is not a backup: it is the only copy of the data, and removing it loses the data.
